extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political economy / public finance; policymakers and historians of economic thought
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for understanding how public debts arise, how states borrow (methods and instruments), and the fiscal, institutional, and social conditions that enable or constrain public borrowing. Focuses on causes, instruments (anticipation, funding, annuities, tontines), and consequences for public revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsimony and saving lead to accumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: In that rude state of society ... the sovereign, it has already been observed ... is in a situation which naturally disposes him to the parsimony requisite for accumulation. The parsimony which leads to accumulation has become almost as rare in republican as in monarchical governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saving/hoarding (by sovereigns or subjects) is the principal means by which treasure is amassed; it is favored by insecurity and the absence of commerce. Where parsimony prevails, public revenue can be freed from extraordinary exigencies; lack of parsimony predisposes a state to borrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial society creates ability and willingness to lend
rubrics_metrics.description: The same commercial state of society which, by the operation of moral causes, brings government in this manner into the necessity of borrowing, produces in the subjects both an ability and an inclination to lend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A country abounding with merchants/manufacturers has circulating capitals that pass through hands many times a year, enabling advances to government; lenders often view lending as increasing their trading capital rather than diminishing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular administration of justice is prerequisite for flourishing commerce (and thus for lending)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce and manufactures can seldom flourish long in any state which does not enjoy a regular administration of justice; in which the people do not feel themselves secure in the possession of their property; in which the faith of contracts is not supported by law; and in which the authority of the state is not supposed to be regularly employed in enforcing the payment of debts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidence in legal enforcement and property rights underpins the willingness of merchants to trust government with loans; weak institutions reduce ability/willingness to lend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate wartime expenses typically require borrowing
rubrics_metrics.description: When war comes, ... an immediate and great expense must be incurred ... that army, that fleet, those garrisoned towns, must be furnished ... An immediate and great expense must be incurred in that moment of immediate danger, which will not wait for the gradual and slow returns of the new taxes. In this exigency, government can have no other resource but in borrowing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax increases take time to produce revenue; therefore governments facing sudden large expenses (war) will generally need to borrow rather than rely on immediate tax revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government reliance on subjects' lending reduces incentive to save
rubrics_metrics.description: The government of such a state is very apt to repose itself upon this ability and willingness of its subjects to lend it their money on extraordinary occasions. It foresees the facility of borrowing, and therefore dispenses itself from the duty of saving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of credit encourages governments to avoid fiscal self-restraint, increasing propensity to contract debt rather than build reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression from unfunded to funded debt via assignments/mortgages
rubrics_metrics.description: Nations, like private men, have generally begun to borrow upon what may be called personal credit, without assigning or mortgaging any particular fund for the payment of the debt; and when this resource has failed them, they have gone on to borrow upon assignments or mortgages of particular funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public debt typically moves from short-term/unfunded obligations toward mortgaging specific revenue streams as earlier informal credit proves insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction and trade-offs: anticipation (short-term) versus perpetual funding
rubrics_metrics.description: When money was raised in the one way, it was said to be raised by anticipation; when in the other, by perpetual funding... If money had never been raised but by anticipation, the course of a few years would have liberated the public revenue ... But the greater part of European governments have been incapable of those attentions... such improvident anticipations necessarily gave birth to the more ruinous practice of perpetual funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipation (short-term tax advances) can free revenue at fixed dates; perpetual funding raises larger immediate sums but postpones permanent liberation of revenue and encourages long-term indebtedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvident anticipation and repeated prolongation overload funds
rubrics_metrics.description: They have frequently overloaded the fund, even upon the first anticipation; and when this happened not to be the case, they have generally taken care to overload it, by anticipating a second and a third time, before the expiration of the first anticipation. The fund becoming in this manner altogether insufficient ... it became necessary to charge it with the interest only ... and such improvident anticipations necessarily gave birth to the more ruinous practice of perpetual funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated short-term borrowing against the same revenue undermines the fund's capacity to pay principal and interest, pushing states toward perpetual annuities and chronic debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sinking fund both relieves debt and facilitates new borrowing
rubrics_metrics.description: A sinking fund, though instituted for the payment of old, facilitates very much the contracting of new debts. It is a subsidiary fund, always at hand, to be mortgaged in aid of any other doubtful fund, upon which money is proposed to be raised in any exigency of the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While intended to amortize debt, sinking funds can be reallocated or mortgaged to secure fresh loans, thus serving as a tool enabling further borrowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borrowing on annuities for terms of years and for lives; tontines raise more money
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides those two methods of borrowing, by anticipations and by a perpetual funding, there are two other methods ... borrowing upon annuities for terms of years, and that of borrowing upon annuities for lives... An annuity for a long term of years, though its intrinsic value may be very nearly the same with that of a perpetual annuity, will not find nearly the same number of purchasers. ... Annuities for lives have occasionally been granted ... either upon separate lives, or upon lots of lives, which, in French, are called tontines ... Upon the same revenue, more money can always be raised by tontines than by annuities for separate lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different annuity forms have varying marketability and raise differing amounts: tontines and survivorship features can be more attractive to governments seeking larger immediate subscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market preferences: perpetual redeemable annuities preferred for transferability
rubrics_metrics.description: The subscribers to a new loan, who mean generally to sell their subscription as soon as possible, prefer greatly a perpetual annuity, redeemable by parliament, to an irredeemable annuity, for a long term of years, of only equal amount. The value of the former may be supposed always the same, or very nearly the same; and it makes, therefore, a more convenient transferable stock than the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liquidity and stable perceived value make perpetual redeemable annuities more attractive to merchant-lenders who plan to resell holdings, influencing the composition of public debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of lenders and seat of government shape debt instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: In England, the seat of government being in the greatest mercantile city in the world, the merchants are generally the people who advance money to government... In France, the seat of government not being in a great mercantile city, merchants do not make so great a proportion of the people who advance money to government. The people concerned in the finances ... make the greater part of those who advance their money in all public exigencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social and geographic composition of typical lenders (merchants vs financiers/farmers-general) affects whether governments issue perpetual annuities, life-annuities, or other instruments, reflecting lenders' investment horizons and motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of interest rates affects annuity burden and creates sinking-fund surplus
rubrics_metrics.description: During the reign of queen Anne, the market rate of interest had fallen from six to five per cent... Soon after the greater part of the temporary taxes of Great Britain had been rendered perpetual ... the creditors of the public ... were induced to accept of five per cent. for the interest of their money, which occasioned a saving of one per cent. ... This saving left a considerable surplus in the produce of the different taxes ... and laid the foundation of what has since been called the sinking fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lowering interest rates on public debt reduces annual annuity costs and can produce a surplus in revenue funds that can be applied to debt reduction—but the surplus may also be used for new borrowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Luxury and courtly expenditure reduce sovereign saving and increase borrowing
rubrics_metrics.description: In a commercial country, abounding with every sort of expensive luxury, the sovereign, in the same manner as almost all the great proprietors in his dominions, naturally spends a great part of his revenue in purchasing those luxuries... The amassing of treasure can no longer be expected; and when extraordinary exigencies require extraordinary expenses, he must necessarily call upon his subjects for an extraordinary aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High consumption of revenues on luxury and pageantry by sovereigns and elites diminishes the capacity to accumulate reserves and raises the likelihood governments will resort to borrowing in crises.
